Ava Patel: Quick follow-up to the ingress abuse fallback sketch in the RFC. Two open questions: should we fallback to a quantized/cheaper model or return soft 429s when a tenant crosses abuse thresholds? Also who owns the probation window metadata (edge vs central)?

Ravi Singh: model fallback keeps UX but risks cost + quality drift. soft 429 is simpler but worse product experience. leaning fallback if we can bound quality regression.

Jules: Agree with Ravi. If we do fallback, add a response header like `X-Fallback-Model` and tag events so downstream can measure quality delta. Also cap max tokens to avoid runaway bills.

Morgan Chen: Security note: fallbacks change execution path. we need to ensure the fallback route still respects KMS key access and audit logging. no silent bypass.

Sam R.: If fallback goes to a shared low-cost pool we should isolate KV cache and prompt contexts per-tenant. Otherwise noisy tenants could pollute cache or cause cross-tenant leaks.

ops-bot: feature-flag created: infra/ingress/fallback-mode.owners=Ava,Ravi :white_check_mark:

Ava Patel: Proposal to discuss: (1) fallback to a quantized model variant that has model-level quality constraints, (2) soft-429 for abuse_score >= 0.8 as a hard guard, (3) probation metadata written to the central admission service with TTL 24h (can be bumped by infra), (4) telemetry required: per-tenant fallback_rate, cost_delta, quality_regression_pct.

Jules: small nit: central probation simplifies reporting but suffers cross-region TTL drift and added RPC on hot path. consider edge-owned probation with periodic flush to central store.

Ravi Singh: tradeoff: edge ownership reduces latency but central ownership enables easier global rollbacks and analytics. if we do edge-first, we need a leader reconciliation to avoid split-brain. etcd leader election or a lightweight lease could work.

Morgan Chen: legal/compliance check: if we route to a lower-quality model that might transform PII differently, do we need to notify customers or update agreements? I can ping legal.

Sam R.: I'll run a canary: enable fallback-mode on staging for a subset of synthetic tenants and measure latency, token counts, and semantic drift using our eval harness. will report numbers in 48h.

Ava Patel: Thanks. Action items: Sam = canary + report; Morgan = legal touchpoint; Ravi/Jules = sketch edge vs central probation flow (callouts for leader election or flush interval). I'll fold decisions back into the RFC and call a quick sync if we need P0 changes.

ops-bot: scheduled: quick-sync with eng-platform on 2026-03-24 16:00 UTC.

Ava Patel: tagging @Jules @Ravi @Sam R. — if anyone has strong objections to central probation TTL=24h default, say now. otherwise i'll update RFC after Sam's canary. :v:
